links.targetTitle: Grove deploys much of its capital through named third-party

title: Two live Morpho instances share the grove-bbqUSDC ticker at different addresses, and their limits do not aggregate by counterparty
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.1.7.1.2.1.4 and A...7.2.2.1.4 both name their token `grove-bbqUSDC`, but the addresses differ: `0xBEEf2B5FD3D94469b7782aeBe6364E6e6FB1B709` for the High Yield Vault and `0xBeefF08dF54897e7544aB01d0e86f013DA354111` for Vault v2 (A...7.1.2.2.1, A...7.2.2.2.1). Both take USDC, both are managed under the same Grove x Steakhouse arrangement, and both are listed Active.

Two consequences follow.

First, the ticker is not an identifier here. Any configuration, monitoring query or reconciliation script keyed on symbol would conflate the two vaults — and they have different rate-limit keys, different protections (only v2 has a `maxExchangeRate`) and different balances. Only the address disambiguates them, which is an argument for treating the address as the primary key in the instance register.

Second, and more substantively: each instance carries an independent 20,000,000 USDC deposit cap with a 20,000,000-per-day slope (A...7.1.2.4.1, A...7.2.2.4.1) and its own pair of RateLimitIDs. Grove's rate limits are keyed per instance, so they do **not** aggregate by manager, strategy, or protocol. Exposure to the Grove x Steakhouse relationship can therefore reach 40 million through two doors, each individually compliant.

This is the structural limitation of instance-level budgeting, and it recurs elsewhere in the register — the four Aave instances are separately capped at 50 million each, and Steakhouse also runs the PYUSD vault in this chunk (A...7.3) at another 20,000,000. The only mechanism seen so far that aggregates across instances is the shared inflow key used by the two Pendle PT instances, which shows the primitive supports counterparty-level caps; here it simply is not used.
description: The v1 and v2 Grove x Steakhouse USDC vaults each carry a 20 million cap with separate rate-limit keys, so one manager relationship can hold twice the per-instance ceiling.
